result.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
result.summary: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. This structure is directly predicted by generative models of user behavior for linear embeddings and extends approximately to deep-learning representations by the superposition hypothesis. Superimposed modes can naturally be recovered by sparse dictionary learning methods, such as sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and recovered modes can be automatically named and queried in natural language. We validate mode recovery against known ground truth on synthetic data, where SAEs recover modes better than classical sparse baselines, including on transformer-encoded embeddings. We then apply the method to classical and transformer-based user embeddings from two real-world datasets. We also show how the corresponding natural-language labels enable zero-shot audience retrieval and characterization over embeddings never trained on text. The framework is post-hoc and model-agnostic, requiring no modification to the upstream embedding system.

AI.brief_summary: 论文论证用户嵌入可看作可解释行为模式的稀疏叠加，用稀疏自编码器恢复这些模式并自动赋予自然语言标签，在合成数据和两个真实数据集上验证，并支持对未训练文本的嵌入做零样本受众检索与刻画。
AI.relevance_reason: 其基于 SAE 的稀疏字典分解与「叠加」视角，可供核查 LVR 内部 latent 状态是否由可解释的视觉细节或几何模式叠加而成、存在多少纠缠与坍缩，但对象是用户行为嵌入，与多模态推理无直接联系，迁移价值需阅读原文确认。
